children: came under pressure Tuesday, with shares down more than 4% before the company reports quarterly results after the market closes.
is signaling an unusually wide potential reaction. Contracts expiring Friday imply a move of about 10%, or roughly $50 based on the stock's price at the time.

Much of the activity is centered on puts, suggesting investors are paying close attention to downside risk. The $400 put had 2,972 contracts outstanding, the largest open position on the chain, while 875 contracts traded during Tuesday's session.
Trading was also active at the $440 put, with 1,574 contracts changing hands against open interest of 1,220. Its premium had risen more than 47% at the time of the report.
Calls indicate that some traders are still positioned for gains. The $500 strike had 2,446 open contracts, followed by 1,093 at $470 and 786 at $430.
The options market points to substantial uncertainty around the earnings reaction, with both bearish protection and upside bets in play.

title: Dell Stock Falls Ahead of Earnings as Options Signal an 10% Swing
